marks.gloss_en: 'one law for the one who acts unwittingly' (Num 15:29) is adjacent to 'the soul that acts with a high hand' (Num 15:30): He juxtaposed unwitting to deliberate -- as the deliberate had knowledge, so the unwitting had knowledge
וכך היה מונבז דן לפני רבי עקיבא -- the unwitting sinner, like the deliberate, is liable only with prior knowledge; the captured child had none
Munbaz: since the deliberate sinner is called 'sinner' and the unwitting one is called 'sinner', as the deliberate one had knowledge, so the unwitting one [is liable only if he] had knowledge
אבל לא שכחה מאי -- חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה? אדתני היודע שהוא שבת... ליתני היודע עיקר שבת, וכל שכן הא -- then the mishna's third clause is the wrong one to teach; אלא מתניתין כשהכיר ולבסוף שכח
the same move (68b.1): it defeats the re-reading that answered 68a.9, and the mishna's one-chatat case becomes the one who knew and forgot -- so he is not liable for each Shabbat
rather, our mishna is [speaking of] one who knew and in the end forgot
מיתיבי (68b.2) ... קתני מיהא כיצד תינוק: בשלמא לרב ושמואל ניחא, אלא לרבי יוחנן ולרבי שמעון בן לקיש קשיא -- the baraita has the captured child liable one chatat
אמרי לך ר' יוחנן ור"ל: לא מי איכא מונבז דפטר? אנן דאמרינן כמונבז -- we said ours in accordance with Munbaz
לדבריך, אין זה קרוי שוגג אלא מזיד -- by your words, one with knowledge at the time of the act is not called unwitting but deliberate
R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish: [liable] specifically one who knew and in the end forgot
the Rabbis need 'one law' (Num 15:29) for what R' Yehoshua ben Levi read to his son
